method.policy: Cross-check TDV, peer-reviewed regional studies, and primary/near-primary chronicle evidence where available. Do not back-project later beylik borders into 1326.
method.politicalControl: Keep direct control, frontier influence, military presence, and trade/merchant presence separate.
method.geometry: No continuous political polygon is promoted from narrative evidence alone. Use city/fort/route anchors and uncertainty bands until date-specific boundary evidence is reconciled.

anchors.name: Kastamonu
evidence: Candaroğlu Süleyman Bey succeeded Yaman Candar and expanded from Eflani to Kastamonu; Kastamonu became the beylik center in the early 14th century.
anchors.guard: Do not use later 14th-century Candar boundaries as the 1326 polygon.

anchors.name: Safranbolu
evidence: Candaroğlu expansion included Safranbolu; later 1332 Ibn Battuta evidence confirms Candar administration.
anchors.guard: Exact 7 April 1326 local boundary remains less certain than Kastamonu/Sinop.

anchors.name: Sinop
evidence: Pervâneoğulları ended in 1322 and Candaroğlu Süleyman Bey incorporated Sinop; independent academic bibliography confirms the 1322 transition.

anchors.name: Bafra-Samsun
evidence: Pervâneoğulları had previously taken Bafra and Samsun, but the polity ended in 1322; later Taceddinoğulları belong to c.1348 onward. Later Ottoman sources describe multiple local political units.
anchors.guard: Do not assign Taceddinoğulları to 1326; do not automatically extend Candar control from Sinop to Samsun.

anchors.name: Ordu-Bayramlu zone
anchors.control1326: Çepni/Türkmen frontier sphere; specific beylik control unresolved
evidence: Academic work places intensive Turkmen military settlement along the Giresun coast in the early 14th century; Hacıemiroğulları are later and should not be back-projected.
anchors.guard: Do not create Hacıemiroğulları polygon for 1326.

anchors.name: Giresun
anchors.control1326: Trabzon Empire city/fortress with active Türkmen frontier pressure
evidence: TDV and Panaretos-based studies describe the 1301 Byzantine/Trabzon counter-campaign and fortification of Giresun; early 14th-century Türkmen activity reached the coastal area.
anchors.guard: Do not equate nearby Türkmen military settlements with permanent political possession of Giresun.

anchors.name: Kuşluhan-Aksu/Dereli zone
anchors.control1326: Türkmen military frontier anchor; exact polity unresolved
evidence: Feridun Emecen identifies Kuşdoğan's influence between Canik and the Giresun Aksu valley and suggests Kuşluhan as a possible military bastion.
anchors.guard: Kuşdoğan is not automatically treated as founder of Hacıemiroğulları.

anchors.name: Trabzon
evidence: The Komnenian state remained centered on Trabzon; western territorial contraction had already removed Sinop and Ordu from durable direct control.
anchors.guard: Keep Ilkhanid influence, trade privileges, and political sovereignty as separate runtime relations.

negativeControls: Pervâneoğulları as an independent polity in 1326
Hacıemiroğulları as a fully formed 1326 polygon
later Candar borders projected unchanged onto 1326

networkLayer.rule: Port status and merchant presence must remain separate from territorial sovereignty.
